# Preflight the whole pane retirement set

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Preflight the entire retirement set before the first tombstone. Permission to
operate on a pane does not establish that its other recorded processes are gone.
A parent harness and its running print-mode child can share a pane but have
different process tuples: excluding the parent's exact tuple still leaves the
live child eligible. One observed-running foreign holder must refuse the whole
takeover before any other holder is changed.

This matters beyond seat availability: registry tombstoning drops pending FYIs
and releases open number claims (the numbers remain burned). Descriptor CAS
protects against snapshot drift; it does not prove a stable holder is safe to
retire. The useful negative regression uses an authorized pane-own-process
caller, a running foreign child, another eligible holder and queued work, then
asserts every record and the queued job are unchanged on refusal.

Keep unknown separate from dead: missing PID, remote ownership and probe failure
cannot justify automatic supersession. Explicit unknown-holder recovery is a
separately authorized operation. An unknown native holder should produce the
pane-recovery refusal, not be masked by a session-resumption hold.

Evidence: #237 reviewed at f62e59ba315e02351a34055dfe5b635782d17481.
crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:623-649 implements the all-holder preflight;
http/identity_tests.rs:2106-2163 pins unchanged holders and queued work.
registration.rs:2692-2724 pins failed-probe refusal ordering.
For prime authority, reuse the existing "Request mutations need bound and
scoped authority" note rather than treating self-role assertions as permission;
#237's designation regression is in http/identity_tests.rs:2013-2072.
